params.echoOutputHighLevel: 5 V TTL, equal to the 5 V supply: needs a divider or level shifter before a 3.3 V GPIO

provenance.notes: KIT: no ultrasonic lesson or part in the SunFounder Basic Starter Kit table of contents or Component List photo, so 'not in kit'. PIN ORDER: the Elecfreaks HC-SR04 datasheet (SparkFun-hosted copy) prints 'Vcc Trig Echo GND' for the four pins and the SunFounder photo shows a 4-pin male header with the same silkscreen (Vcc, Trig, Echo, Gnd), so Dupont male-female leads go female end onto the module. SUPPLY: the datasheet 'Electric Parameter' table gives Working Voltage DC 5 V and Working Current 15 mA, with no tolerance range, so vccMinV and vccMaxV are both 5. ECHO LEVEL (important): the datasheet says only 'Echo Output Signal: Input TTL lever signal and the range in proportion', with the module powered from 5 V; it prints no voltage number for ECHO. The 5 V level is therefore an inference from the 5 V TTL supply, confirmed by two tutorials that state it outright: wiki.e-yantra.org ('ECHO outputs 5V. Use a voltage divider (1kOhm + 2kOhm) to bring it down to 3.3V before connecting to the Pi GPIO') and pimylifeup.com ('the HC-SR04 outputs at 5V which can damage the Raspberry Pi'). This is why ECHO needs a divider or level shifter before a 3.3 V GPIO (SPEC 8 OVERVOLTAGE_GPIO, SPEC 13.1 ultrasonic assertion). TRIGGER: datasheet 'Trigger Input Signal: 10uS TTL pulse' and 'IO trigger for at least 10us high level'; the module then sends eight 40 kHz pulses; distance = echo high time x 340 m/s / 2, or us / 58 = cm; use a measurement cycle over 60 ms (SunFounder repeats this). The datasheet gives no TRIG input threshold voltage, so none is recorded. RANGE: 2 cm to 400 cm, accuracy to 3 mm, measuring angle 15 degrees; the datasheet lists 'Working Frequency 40Hz', which is a typo for the 40 kHz burst (the same sheet says 40 kHz in the principle text). SIZE: 'Dimension 45*20*15mm' from the datasheet. The transducer diameter and spacing are measured from the SunFounder photo using the 45 mm board length as the scale (+-1 mm) and are stored under 'Approx' keys. The datasheet's attention note says to connect GND first when hot-plugging. LOOK: Adafruit's photos (3942-01, 3942-02) and the Cytron manual (product layout and drawing) show a blue board with two aluminium cans, their mesh fronts inside a rolled rim, about 12 mm tall, their centres about 8.3 mm from the header's edge; an HC-49/S crystal between them at the far edge; the legend HC-SR04 under it, T and R at the near corners and Vcc, Trig, Echo, Gnd up from the pins; four 1 mm holes 1.4 mm in from the ends (Cytron draws them 40 mm apart, the photo 42 mm); on the back three small-outline chips (two 14-lead, one 16-lead) and their passives. The header is right-angle, its black base on the back at the near edge and its pins leaving the board's edge parallel to it, so the module lies on its back with the pins along -y.
